text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- The government's pension reform plan was heavily criticised by all opposition parties in Parliament on Wednesday, as was expected, but also encountered objections from some Socialist MPs.
- A spate of agreements, altogether seven, were signed in Budapest Wednesday during the first visit by Moldavian Prime Minister Ion Ciubuc to Hungary.

- Foreign Ministry spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi was on Wednesday approved by Parliament's foreign affairs committee as Hungary's next ambassador to London. He will replace retiring ambassador Tade Alfoldy.
- The finance ministry and the EU Economic and Financial Directorate have preparad a joint study on Hungary's medium-term economic priorities.
-This year's real wage increase will permit an overall 21 percent pension increase next year, Welfare Minister Mihaly Kokeny told reporters.
- The board of directors of privatisation agency APV Rt will propose a buyout of Alitalia's 35 percent stake in the state airlines Malev.

- Thegovernment policy of maintaining a minimum state holding of 25 percent plus one vote or 50 percent plus one vote in strategic companies was abandoned in favour of "golden shares" granting special ownership rights, State privatisation agency APV Rt chief Pal Szabo told a news conference.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The Budapest Prosecutor General's office plans to file charges against former Socialist Party treasurer Laszlo Boldvai and eight others for their involvement in the Tocsik scandal.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- The order of the turnover tax on businesses is to change from January 1, 1998, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy told tne newspaper.
- Local councils in souther Hungary will offer their combined four percent or 1.2 billion forint face value stake in the south Transdanubian electricity supplier Dedasz.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- A limited company will be founded in early July to manage the construction of a fourth metro line in Budapest, municipal councillor Laszlo Gulyas told the newspaper.

- Privatisation agency APV's board approved a privatisation strategy for the broadcasting company Antenna Hungaria, according to which Antenna's primary capital will be raised to 10.35 billion forints by the end of June, following a 2.5 billion forint raise by the APV in two stages. (Also in Vilaggazdasag)
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Capital investments by domestic investors into foreign countries totalled $50 million in the first quarter, as against $67 million in the whole of last year, the National Bank of Hungary reveals.
